summary: Temporary rear-wheel drive for xDrive cars, from the iDrive 6 menu
author: inotbarnacle (packaged by NBTApps)
description:
A menu under My Vehicle that asks the stability control unit (DSC) of an xDrive car for rear-wheel drive until the ignition is next switched off. The author calls it experimental.

What it does
- Switches between AWD and RWD. The second selection confirms the request
- Works only with the DSC versions 0F2510 and 0F2850, and 0F1860 (the F-series DSC_25) with the transfer case LMV 0F1480. With any other, or with no reply from the DSC, it sends nothing
- Before it sends the request it checks that the car is in Park and the speed is zero, and that the engine is off, or on DSC 0F1860 that it is running
- Checks the transfer case before it reports that the change was made
- Status tells apart a DSC that does not answer, one that refuses, and one it does not support

What you need
- An NBT Evo head unit with iDrive 6 (ID6), on a software version the app was built for (see Good to know)
- NBTApps agent 1.6.0 or later
- The car's diagnostic gateway. The app tries 169.254.21.3, and if nothing answers there, looks for the gateway on the car's wired network
- An xDrive car with one of the three supported DSC versions
- A car that reports Park to the app. One that does not cannot switch

After installing
The iDrive screen restarts. Open My Vehicle and choose xDrive Control. Apply the parking brake before you confirm a switch.

Good to know
- On DSC 0F2510 and 0F2850 the engine must be off to switch from AWD to RWD or back. On DSC 0F1860 it must be running
- RWD is temporary. Switch the ignition off and on to get AWD back, or use the restore button on DSC 0F2850 or 0F1860
- Switch back to AWD before you remove the package
- It does not flash the transfer case and has no calibration options
- The author's notes say the app still needs to be proven on compatible xDrive cars. Rear-wheel drive changes how the car handles: this is at your own risk more than most
- It needs the diagnostic gateway and does not fall back to the car's MOST bus
- This package does not check the head unit's software version. The author's own installer checks the head unit's iDrive framework files, and accepts those of these NBTevo versions only: K17052I, L17252I, M17345I, M17365I, N18032I, N18092I, O18184I, P18362I, Q18491I, R19101I, R19144I, S19221I, S19322I, T18501I, T21424I, T23235J, T24081I, U19384I, V20153I, W20204I, X20511I, Y21432J, Y22292I, Y23236I and Y24073J. On another version the menu may not load
- If the app was put on this car before, with the author's desktop installer or by hand, uninstall it the same way first. NBTApps refuses to install over it
- If the app does not find the car's diagnostic gateway, put its address in a gateway-ip.txt file on the head unit: /var/opt/hmi/data/ID5/gateway-ip.txt for all of the author's apps at once, or one in the app's own folder. The shared file comes first. This package writes neither
- This is a pre-release: the package has not yet been installed on a car through NBTApps

xDrive Control is by inotbarnacle, free of charge under the MIT License. Its DSC commands come from the idrive7-apps project, whose licence is in the package. NBTApps packages the author's own builds, unchanged, with the author's agreement. It comes as it is: you install it at your own risk.
